page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.16-128 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine provisioned from the Standard instance family. Compute capacity is driven by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor running at a clock speed of 2.55 GHz. The configuration allocates 16 dedicated physical cores and 32 virtual CPUs utilizing simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core. System memory is sized at 128.0 GB, establishing a balanced profile of 4.0 GB per virtual processor.

The instance relies entirely on network-attached storage for non-volatile data persistence, as no local disk storage is bundled with the hardware profile. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included in the configuration. Network addressing includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the CPU allocation is dedicated rather than shared or burstable, the instance avoids host-level resource contention, maintaining consistent CPU cycles under sustained load.

VM.Standard.E4.Flex.16-128 provides predictable, linear resource scaling for tasks that match standard enterprise density without requiring high memory-per-core premiums or specialized graphics hardware. Appropriate workload fits include intermediate relational database hosting, container cluster worker nodes, enterprise application servers, and continuous integration environments.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.16-128 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor operating at a base clock frequency of 2.55 GHz, configured with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via two threads per core. CPU allocation is fully dedicated, ensuring consistent computational execution without resource contention from neighboring tenants. Paired with the compute configuration is 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual core. The instance includes no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent data. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for external network connectivity. VM.Standard.E4.Flex.16-128 offers balanced resource allocation suitable for enterprise application hosting, batch processing, mid-tier relational database systems, and general containerized microservices requiring predictable thread scheduling.
